title: Tenant-partitioned tracing, log-shredding, and cost-aware composite SLOs for console analytics
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: Our analytics ingest pipeline and console backend generate high-cardinality traces and verbose tenant logs. Cost growth for observability storage is outpacing feature adoption for low-volume tenants, and current SLIs are siloed per-service, making end-to-end degradation hard to diagnose. Goals: 1) Provide tenant-partitioned tracing so we can correlate client requests across the ingest pipeline while enforcing per-tenant quotas and adaptive sampling. 2) Implement log-shredding/redaction and per-tenant retention bands to reduce storage costs and compliance risk. 3) Define and implement composite SLOs that combine stage-specific SLIs (ingest latency, transform throughput, storage write error rate) into tenant-level health signals used by console dashboards and alerting. Scope: - Instrument trace propagation across frontend -> kafka ingestion -> transform -> metrics writer, with tenant-aware sampling tags. - Add a log-shredding pipeline stage that strips PII and moves high-cardinality fields to a cheaper object store for on-demand retrieval. - Implement adaptive retention policies (hot/medium/cold) driven by tenant usage tiers and synthetic probe scoring. - Create new dashboards and SLO rules in the console and wire up automated incident tags for downstream runbooks. Non-goals: full trace rehydration for cold-storage logs in this ticket (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Trace context propagates across all ingest stages with tenant_id and observability_lane tags in at least 90% of sampled requests
Log-shredding reduces average per-tenant log size by >= 40% for low-volume tenants without losing required audit fields
Composite SLOs computed for at least two pilot tenants and reflect combined latency + error budget with documented burn policies
Dashboards display per-tenant SLO status and cost-estimated retention tier with drilldowns to trace samples
Kubernetes and Kafka configs include safety knobs to limit observability ingestion on a per-tenant basis to prevent noisy tenants from impacting others

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overaggressive sampling may hide rare but critical failures. Mitigation: implement adaptive tail-sampling and synthetic probes to preserve coverage.
Risk: Shredding could accidentally remove fields needed for audits. Mitigation: schema-driven shredding with whitelist for compliance fields + legal review for EU tenants.
Risk: Per-tenant quotas might impact high-volume customers unexpectedly. Mitigation: rollout as opt-in for pilots, expose throttling metrics and graceful degradation fallbacks.
